title: Counter-Attack Transition
content: A counter-attack exploits the disorganised defensive state of the opponent immediately after possession is won. Speed of transition is the primary weapon: the first touch after winning possession should already be directed forward where possible. Key decisions in the first 3–5 seconds: (1) can I play forward immediately to a running teammate? (2) do I carry the ball to buy time for runners? (3) is the opportunity genuine or should we consolidate? False counter-attacks (slow transitions) gift the opponent time to reorganise and are often worse than consolidating possession. The ideal counter-attack has 2–3 players in forward positions against 2 or fewer defenders, exploiting the channel between full-back and center-back.
